doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Group playing, Town Hall and the White House
title: What kinds of groups he prefers

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: There are a couple of groups that you have that have a simpatico… I’m thinking of a lot of dates both recording and live that you’ve done with, let’s say, the Don Thompson and Terry Clarke…
…(trio?). I guess I wonder, you know, what… And, and again, I have a feeling that a lot of the questions about music are not easy to put into words.
Well, more than that, there’s kind of questions having to do with humanity or people getting along or not getting along personally because that’s…
Well, for instance, are there some groups or ensembles or people that you work with that are more fun and this person is more classic and this group has more of an adventure bent…
Or this one can be more avant-garde-ish or…
And do you have a preference?

Well, I guess especially what I just said about Metheny… I guess my preference would be to… not necessarily avant-garde, but to kinda be open to changes and things like that and… Again, it has to do with humans interacting and… I’m trying to remember classic… Oh. (laughs) I did… Who was I working with? This string group someplace. Oh, I know what it was. I played a piece of Don Erb’s.
